1. The present petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of the Fir No.
357/2022 under Sections 498A/406/34 Ipc registered at P.S. Aman Vihar alongwith all other
proceedings emanating therefrom, on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
2. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He submits that since the aforesaid FIR is an outcome of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have arrived at a settlement, the State has no objection in case the FIR in question is quashed.
3. The learned APP further apprises the court that the case is still at the stage of investigation and chargesheet has not yet been filed.

4. The petitioner no. 1 (former husband), the petitioner no. 2 and 3 who are the parents of the petitioner no. 1, as well as, the respondent no. 2 (former wife) are present in court and they have been identified by their

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/10/2023 at 07:40:10 respective counsels, as well as, by the Investigating Officer, SI Karamveer Singh, P.S. Aman Vihar.
5. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 06.10.2019 as per Hindu Rites and Ceremonies at Delhi.
Out of the said wedlock, one female minor child namely Baby Krishti was born on 23.02.2021.

However, on account of temperamental differences, the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 started living separately w.e.f. 07.01.2021.
6.
Further, the disputes between the parties led to certain litigations between them including the registration of the aforesaid FIR.

sentences.text:
During the pendency of the proceedings, the matter was referred to Delhi Mediation Centre,
Rohini District Courts, Delhi where a settlement was arrived at between the parties, the terms of which were recorded in writing on 26.08.2022.
8.

In terms of the said settlement, it was agreed between the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 that the parties shall get their marriage dissolved by obtaining a decree of divorce by way of mutual consent.
9. The learned counsel for the parties informs that the marriage between the parties has already been dissolved by decree of divorce by mutual consent dated 17.12.2022.

10. It was further agreed between the parties that the petitioner no. 1 shall pay an amount of Rs.
2,50,000/- to the respondent no. 2 towards full and final settlement of her claims on account of Stree Dhan, maintenance (past, present and future), permanent alimony etc.
11.

Out of the settlement amount, the petitioner no. 1 has already paid an amount of Rs. 2,00,000/-
at the stages mentioned in the settlement This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/10/2023 at 07:40:10 agreement, the receipt of which the respondent no. 2 acknowledges.

The balance amount of Rs.
50,000/- has been paid by the petitioner 1 to respondent no. 2 in court today by way of demand draft no. 424946 dated 19.05.2023 drawn on Central Bank of India, SSB Delhi-2332.
12.
The respondent no. 2 who is present in court submits that she has no objection in case the aforesaid FIR is quashed.
13. In view of the facts that the parties have arrived at a settlement, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
14. It is, thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and the proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.
15. Consequently, the petition is allowed and FIR No. 357/2022 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at P.S. Aman Vihar alongwith all other proceedings emanating therefrom, is quashed.
16. The petition is disposed of.
17. Order be uploaded on the website of this court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J MAY 31, 2023 N.S. ASWAL
